answer: Each agent locks an 80-credit bond on one timber-framed glacier gauge at one channel. The gauge records shift in a 14-field gale log of wind, depth, sediment, melt, so a short reading breaks the form. An auditor recomputes it from the melt table and gauge serial; a mismatch or reused serial burns the bond. The first gauge costs 32, the kth 32+7(k-1), the 1000th 7025, so 1000 false gauges cost 3,528,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails: each serial binds one channel and one epoch, so a copied log repeats a serial. An honest agent pays 32 once and keeps the bond after an audit.
